Remediation engine · follow-up benchmark · 2026-10-08

Engine Benchmark Re-run

The real engine code (main, 7b2c10c) was run on all 10,048 CVEs of the first benchmark and compared three ways: the research expectation from that benchmark, the scanner's remediations (DB), and the engine's output today.

Summary

85.4%8,582 CVEs get the same actions the research expected; 9,520 (94.7%) keep the same verdict
70.8%7,115 CVEs where engine and scanner agree or are equivalent
28.2%2,833 CVEs where the scanner is better, including 1,934 where the engine is silent
60CVEs where the engine is better than the scanner

Where the scanner is better, 79.8% of the cases (2,261) trace back to the early stage: prerequisite mapping, catalog records and tags. 569 (20.1%) are engine logic, and 381 of those are one new rule misfiring on Chrome.

Findings, by impact

1,934CVEs, engine silent

Ignore-tagged components still silence a fifth of the CVEs

Unchanged since the research. chromium-browser alone covers 1,726 of them; the scanner names Chrome or Edge. Early stage: tagging and prerequisite mapping.

Retag chromium-browser Non-OS and resolve it to the installed browser, or map these CVEs to google-chrome / microsoft-edge.

381CVEs, new regression

"Remove Google Chrome" on every Chrome CVE

The retired-product rule (every release line end of life → remove-component) fired for Chrome: on 2026-10-08 endoflife.date lists all 147 Chrome lines as end of life, because 154 ended 2026-10-06 and 155 is not listed yet. The research and the scanner both say update Chrome. Engine logic.

Treat a product as retired only when its newest line ended more than a set time ago (for example 90 days), or when it is also in DISCONTINUED.

186CVEs

Prerequisites point at the wrong component

Same as the research: for example MSMQ instead of IBM WebSphere MQ, legacy Edge CVEs mapped to Chromium Edge. Early stage: prerequisite mapping.

Fix the mappings listed under this cause in the explorer.

166CVEs

Ignore + OS falls back to an OS update

When the only product is Ignore-tagged, the OS becomes the target. The scanner names the browser update. Engine logic.

When Ignore components are set aside, keep the OS as context and give no software path.

96CVEs, new

Java sub-components marked discontinued get "remove"

Deployment Toolkit, browser plugin and Web Start CVEs are fixed by JRE updates, and these pieces cannot be removed on their own. The CVEs are tagged only with the sub-component, never Java SE. Early stage: the DISCONTINUED list and tagging.

Take these three out of DISCONTINUED, or tag Java SE on their CVEs so the engine gives the JRE update.

972CVEs, improved

New rules that work

931 Flash, Shockwave and Equation Editor CVEs now get "remove", which the scanner also says (uninstall). 41 CVEs whose component has no catalog record now get an update that matches the scanner, where the research engine had nothing.

Merging identical OS updates changed the wording of 156 CVEs and no verdict.

16CVEs

Vector products fixed instead of the real one

Python next to Firefox, Outlook next to a Windows OLE bug: the engine adds an update for the carrier. Engine logic (runtime and vector handling).

Treat runtimes and vector products as context when another product is present.

Smaller items: the samba slug returns 404 on endoflife.date, so Samba gets no EOL check.

Versions and end of life in the scanner data

37.6%3,782 CVEs where the scanner names the affected version line (Windows 10 1607, Tomcat 8.5, el7). 37.8% of CVEs with scanner data.
25.9%2,601 CVEs where at least one named line is end of life. 68.8% of the CVEs that name a line.
82.3%8,265 CVEs with any version number, including fixed-in versions only
34.4%3,460 CVEs naming an end-of-life line or a discontinued product (Flash, AIR, Silverlight)

The affected-line count is a floor. A check of 60 random CVEs against the extraction found 3 misses and no false hits (Java "8 Update 65", Ubuntu package names like postgresql-client-14). Correcting for that rate gives about 4,197 CVEs (41.8%). In that sample, 30 of 60 CVEs give only a fixed-in version. End-of-life status comes from the first benchmark's verified list of 147 product lines (2026-10-04).

Compared with the research expectation

8,582 CVEs (85.4%) get exactly the actions the research simulated. The other 1,466 changed for three reasons: discontinued products now get "remove" (1,035), the retired-product rule on Chrome (381), and components without a catalog record now get an update (50).

Method and limits

  • Engine: the repository's engine/ and defs/ at main 7b2c10c, run on every CVE of the first benchmark, with prerequisites from db/cve_to_prereq_with_ids.csv.
  • That CSV has no parameters, so no versions and no network direction. The per-version EOL check did not run; the product-level "all lines end of life" check did. Network options default to incoming.
  • endoflife.date was read for the 50 products the engine looked up, by two subagents, on 2026-10-08. Only Chrome came back fully end of life; samba returned 404.
  • For CVEs whose actions match the research simulation, the research verdict and root cause carry over. The 110 changed CVEs that no longer matched the scanner were judged in 13 groups by a subagent; Chrome (381) and the matching cases were classified by rule.
  • Engine vs scanner matching reuses the first benchmark's template classes and component–product pairs.
  • Version and EOL figures use regular-expression extraction from scanner texts, checked on a 60-CVE sample by a subagent.
